Sabit fiyatlarla GSYH: Or real GDP: the national income method measuring the value of the goods and services produced in a given period at the prices of a fixed base year.
Sabit gider endüstrisi: An industry in which firms' average total cost does not change as the market grows.
Sabit girdi: Or a fixed factor: the production factors whose quantity cannot be changed in a given period.
Sabit kur rejimi: An exchange rate regime in which the nominal exchange rates are determined by the state, and the central bank intervenes in the market in order to keep the rate at a fixed level.
Sabit sermaye: Or a fixed asset: the durable goods such as machinery, factories, vehicles and buildings produced to generate income in the future.
Sabit sermaye tüketimi: Or depreciation: the wear-and-tear or aging share of physical capital.
Saf oligopol: An oligopoly market in which a homogeneous product is bought and sold.
Sahiplik etkisi: A person's assigning to an asset it owns a higher value than it would pay if it did not own it; it delays the sale.
Sahte Banknot: The banknote whose counterfeitness is established by a court decision.
Saklama Hizmeti: The services relating to the capital market instruments deposited or delivered, by book entry or physically, in connection with capital market activities — whether by reason of capital market activities, or in the capacity of custodian, or for administration, or as collateral, or under whatever name — to the capital market instruments.
Samurai Bonds: The securities issues made in Japan, in Japanese yen, by foreigners. They are mostly issues with maturities of 5 years and over. The first issue was made in 1970 by the Asian Development Bank.
Sanayi kümelenmesi: The more effective working of interrelated firms using similar infrastructure and production factors by gathering in a certain geographical region.
Sanayi Odası: The professional organizations possessing legal personality and of the nature of public institutions, established by law with the aim of ensuring solidarity among industrialists, working for the solution of their common problems, and protecting their common interests.
Sanayi Sicil Belgesi: A document given to the industrial enterprises evaluated within the scope of Article 1 of the Industrial Registry Law No. 6948, and to the enterprises making continuous and serial repairs and the large construction sites such as power plants producing electricity or other energy and shipbuilding, which must be obtained within 2 (two) months from the date on which the enterprise began its production activity. The said document is drawn up by the Provincial Directorates of Industry and Technology.
Sanayi Üretim Endeksi - SÜE: An index calculated monthly in order to measure the short-term positive or negative effects of the developments occurring in the economy and of the economic policies implemented. According to the NACE Rev.2 classification, it covers the sectors of mining and quarrying, manufacturing, and the production and distribution of electricity, gas, steam and air conditioning.
Satım Opsiyonu: It expresses the right to sell. It gives the party holding the option contract the right to sell the instrument underlying the option under the conditions stated in the option, but brings no obligation. Depending on market conditions, the party holding the option may not exercise the option. The exercise of the option is expressed as being 'exercised'. The party selling the option, on the other hand, is obliged to fulfill the terms of the contract if the buying party wants to exercise the option.
Satın Alma Gücü Paritesi: The exchange rate that equalizes the prices of similar goods and services subject to trade in a certain basket across different countries. Since, in calculating purchasing power parity, only the goods and services subject to trade are taken into consideration, such a calculation can fall short of measuring the true value of the rate of exchange between the two countries' currencies.
Satın Alma Yöneticileri Endeksi: A diffusion index obtained from the answers the purchasing managers of industrial firms give to questions about the development of production, orders, employment, suppliers' delivery times and input stocks.
Satış: The price at which the market participants are willing to sell the values traded in the market (such as foreign currency and securities).
Search Warrant Yetkili mercii: (the judge) The permission given by the competent authority for the security forces to conduct a search. SECI (Southeast European Cooperation Initiative): the Southeast European Cooperation Initiative established pursuant to the 'Agreement on Cooperation to Combat Transborder Crime' signed in Bucharest on 26 May 1999. The aim of the Initiative is for the party countries to assist one another in the prevention, detection, investigation and prosecution of transborder crimes. The Initiative, headquartered in Bucharest,
Second Best: The level closest to the conditions of full competition. One of the most important justifications of competition policies is the thought that the fully competitive market leads societies to the highest welfare level, the 'first best'. However, it is known that full competition is a utopian model and that, in practice, it will not be possible to satisfy the conditions of full competition. For this reason, the aim of competition policies is to minimize the departures from the rules of full competition so that social welfare rises to the highest possible level — that is, the 'second best'
Sektörel Dış Ticaret Şirketi: The companies established in order to enable the enterprises in the same production field to open up to their foreign markets by uniting under an organization for the purpose of exporting.
Selective Pricing: The selective low pricing, independent of costs, among customers or products, undertaken by the undertakings in a dominant position with the aim of making their rivals' activities difficult.
Senyoraj - Beylik Hakkı: The real revenue the institution holding the authority to print money obtains by printing money by virtue of this authority. It is expressed as the ratio of the change in the money stock to the general price level. In the case where inflation stems only from the increase in the quantity of money, seigniorage and the inflation tax equal one another.
Serbest Dalgalı Kur Rejimi: Refers to the system in which the exchange rate is determined according to the supply and demand conditions in the market. Central banks never intervene in the market, or very rarely, only in extraordinary conditions.
Serbest piyasa ekonomisi: The economic system in a country in which decisions on what to produce, how, and for whom are taken as a result of the interaction of buyers and sellers in the markets.
Serbest rezerv: The reserves a bank holds in addition to its required reserve amount.
Serbest Yatırım Fonu: Refers to a type of investment fund whose certain restrictions have been minimized and in which as flexible an investment strategy as possible can be followed. The fundamental difference of hedge funds from ordinary investment funds is the possibilities of short selling and of borrowing (being able to invest with borrowed resources). Furthermore, thanks to hedge funds, the investor can take short and long positions, apply arbitrage strategies, at the same time both buy and sell a security priced below its value, invest in options or bonds, and invest in any kind of market carrying the possibility of obtaining high returns under low risk.
Sermaye arzı: Or in short SK: the total quantity of capital that all the units in the economy want to rent out, depending on the interest rate, in a given period.
Sermaye Hesabı: It contains the flows arising through the acquisition and disposal of non-produced, non-financial assets (intangible assets such as a piece of land, and intangible assets such as franchises, trademarks and leases — transferable contracts) and capital transfers (such as debt forgiveness and other capital transfers).
Sermaye kaçışı: The international capital flows taking place outside the knowledge and supervision of the state.
Sermaye Koruma Tamponu: Refers to the additional core capital amount that banks are expected to hold, with the aim of preventing equity from falling short of the regulations on capital adequacy owing to the losses that may be encountered in the event of the deterioration of the economic and financial indicators.
Sermaye Piyasası: The markets in which investment instruments with maturities longer than one year are issued and traded.
Sermaye piyasası dengesi: The situation in which, in a given period, the quantity of capital demanded in the market equals the quantity of capital supplied.
Sermaye talebi: Or in short DK: the total quantity of capital that all the units in the economy want to rent, depending on the interest rate, in a given period.
Sermayenin kira oranı: Or in short PK: the payment made for using one unit of capital in production.
Sermayenin marjinal ürün geliri: Or in short MRPK: the change seen in total revenue when the quantity of capital is increased by one unit.
Sermayenin marjinal ürünü: Or in short MPK: the change seen in the total quantity of product when the quantity of capital is increased by one unit.
Sermayenin ortalama ürünü: Or in short APK: the quantity of product produced per unit of capital in a given period.
Sharing Economy: The sharing economy is an economic system based on the foundation of a good or service being shared by its owner, for a fee or free of charge, over an online platform. The sharing economy refers to the renting or sharing of goods rather than their purchase. In the sharing economy, the owner of a good, such as a house, a car or a bicycle, rents out a good it is not using to another person for a temporary period. The online platforms on which the sharing transaction is carried out depend on people being able to trust one another
Sharpe oranı: The ratio of the portfolio's excess return to its standard deviation: (Rp − Rf) / σp. It measures the premium per unit of total risk; beta is not used.
Sigorta: The service of providing financial protection against various risks.
Sigorta piyasası: The physical or virtual environment where insurance policies are bought and sold, and in this process the insurance premium rates are determined.
Sigorta poliçesi: The contract giving the assurance of a certain payment in the event of the realization of predetermined damages and losses.
Sigorta primi: The payment made in return for the insurance policy.
Single Unit Discounts: If the rebate systems applied by undertakings are made conditional on the buyer's fulfilling the purchase condition relating to a single product/market, such rebates are called 'single-product rebates'. For example, a tire shop's earning a premium in return for making a certain amount of sales annually is a kind of single-product rebate.
Sistem riski: The risk of payment disruptions arising across the financial system because of adverse economic developments.
Sistematik risk: The risk affecting the market as a whole and not eliminable by diversification (interest, inflation and exchange rate shocks); beta measures this risk.
Sistemik Risk: The interruption of financial services, in a part of or the whole financial system, in a way that can also lead to serious adverse consequences on economic activity, is called systemic risk. Whether any financial institution's financial insufficiency is a source of systemic risk depends on the effect stemming from this insufficiency being able to spread to the whole of the financial system and hence to the economy in general.
Sonuç: The measurable, concrete situations expected to form within 1-3 years following the completion of the project, obtained in line with the specific aims determined at the outset. Social Enterprise: the type of venture that aims to make profit but uses the profit it obtains to produce benefit for society. Social Innovation: the term for the innovative works used in addressing the problems and needs arising in societies.
